topic.title: Fired And Funded In The Same Week
topic.claim: One company cut a third of its India staff and another Indian startup became a billion-dollar company in the same week, and both headlines are the same economy talking.
topic.behaviour: Oracle sent termination emails to roughly 10,000 of its ~30,000 India employees; days later, AI infra startup Blacksmith raised money at a $1 billion valuation.
topic.mechanism: Capital is concentrating on a handful of big AI bets while big companies use the same AI story to justify thinning teams that now look replaceable.
topic.group: anyone deciding between a 'stable' corporate job and a startup offer this year
topic.moment: You scroll past a unicorn announcement right after reading that layoffs just hit a company everyone called safe.

turn.believed: A big corporate job is the safe bet, a startup is the risky gamble.
turn.actually: This year the 'safe' job is the one getting cut in bulk, and the 'risky' bet is the one pulling in fresh funding.

topic.because: Investors are putting money behind fewer, bigger AI bets, while large companies use the same AI wave to justify shrinking headcount.

proof.fact: Around 10,000 Oracle employees in India — roughly one-third of its ~30,000-person India workforce — received termination emails
Blacksmith...raised $66 million at a $1 billion valuation to become India's latest unicorn

topic.payoff: Ask yourself which one you still call 'safe' without checking the date on that belief.
topic.send_to: Send to the friend weighing a startup offer against a 'stable' MNC job right now.
real_details: Qualcomm's CEO announced 'performance-focused' layoffs the same week
around 12,700 Indian tech workers returned from the US by September 2026
topic.news_peg: Oracle's ~10,000-person India layoff and Blacksmith's unicorn round, both reported the week of October 21-23, 2026
topic.why_now: Both landed in the same seven days, which almost never happens this visibly.

score.why: The safe-job-vs-startup instinct gets flipped hard by one week's headlines, a genuinely surprising reframe for anyone weighing an offer.
